body.statement:
Let \(m=|\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}|\), \(p=2K\), \(\epsilon_q=e_q/\sigma_q\), and
\[
 S_{n,k}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}\epsilon_q.
\]
Indexing \(q\) arbitrarily, sign-expand
\[
 X_q=\sqrt m\,(a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q,
 -a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,-a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q)\in\mathbb R^p.
\]
Then \(m^{-1/2}\sum_qX_q\) has maximum \(\max_k|S_{n,k}|\), every coordinate has variance one, and \(\max_{q,j}\|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\sqrt m L_n(K)\).  For \(0<\gamma<1/2\), put
\[
 \mathfrak g_n(\gamma)=C_1\left[
 \{L_n(K)^2\log^7(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)\}^{1/8}
 +L_n(K)\log^2(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)+\gamma\right],
\]
where \(C_1\) depends only on \(C_e\).  If \(M_n^Z=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|Z_{n,k}|\), then
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|\le z\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}|
 \le\mathfrak g_n(\gamma).
\]
Fix \(C>0\) and \(h\ge0\).  Let \(\mathcal A_n(C)\) be as in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-influence}\), let \(\mathcal B_n(h)=\{r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\le h\}\), and put \(\delta_h=2h+h^2\).  There are constants \(C_2,C_3<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\), such that whenever \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 \mathfrak c_n(h):=C_3\delta_h^{1/3}
 \{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3},
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n\!\left\{
 \max_k\frac{|\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}|}{\widehat s_k}\le z
 \right\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|\\
 &\quad\le \mathfrak g_n(\gamma)+P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 +P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}
 +C_2\{C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}
 +\delta_h\log(2p)\}+\mathfrak c_n(h).
 \end{aligned}
\]
On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), conditionally on \(Y\), \(W_n^\xi\) is exactly the maximum absolute coordinate of \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\), and
\[
 \sup_z|P(W_n^\xi\le z\mid Y)-P(M_n^Z\le z)|
 \le \mathfrak c_n(h).
\]
If \(\mathfrak c_n(h)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\), then the band satisfies the finite coverage bound
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|P_n\{\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\in\mathcal C_{n,k}
 \text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K_n\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\\
 &\quad\le 1\wedge\Big[\mathfrak g_n(\gamma)
 +P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}+2P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}+C_2\{C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}
 +\delta_h\log(2p)\}+2\mathfrak c_n(h)\Big].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Define \(\mathfrak c_n(0)=0\).  Consequently, along any complete array in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), if for some fixed \(C\) and some deterministic \(h_n\downarrow0\),
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(2p)\to0,
\]
then the conditional multiplier distribution consistently estimates the Gaussian comparison law and the displayed band has coverage tending to \(1-\alpha\).  This corollary is conditional on the two displayed failure probabilities; the frozen class alone does not make them vanish.
body.justification: This theorem gives an explicit finite-error whole-curve guarantee while keeping the two unproved growing-block controls visible as failure probabilities.
body.gap: Scalar Choi--Yuan inference and generic Gaussian approximation do not imply feasible growing-path coverage without simultaneous remainder and score-loading control.
body.consumer: Researchers can use the bound to justify one right-to-carry event-curve critical value only after verifying or imposing rates that make the displayed failure terms vanish.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(s_k^2=\sum_qc_{kq}^2\sigma_q^2\) and
\(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\), assumption
\(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) gives
\[
 \sum_qa_{kq}^2=1.
\]
Assumptions \(\texttt{ass:centered-errors}\) and
\(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\) imply that the sign-expanded vectors
\(X_q\) are independent and centered.  Since
\(E_{P_n}\epsilon_q^2=1\), for each of their \(p=2K\) coordinates,
\[
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^2=\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1.
\]
Their normalized sum has coordinate list
\((S_{n,0},\ldots,S_{n,K-1},-S_{n,0},\ldots,-S_{n,K-1})\), so its maximum
is \(\max_k|S_{n,k}|\).  Finally,
\(\|\epsilon_q\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\) and \(|a_{kq}|\le L_n(K)\) prove
the stated envelope.

We now verify the quantitative input to
\(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-approximation-maxima}\).  In the notation of that
cited theorem, let
\[
 M_\ell=\max_{j\le p}
 \left(m^{-1}\sum_qE_{P_n}|X_{qj}|^\ell\right)^{1/\ell}.
\]
Uniform sub-Gaussian moments and \(\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M_3^3
 &\le C m^{1/2}\max_k\sum_q|a_{kq}|^3
 \le C m^{1/2}L_n(K),\\
 M_4^4
 &\le C m\max_k\sum_qa_{kq}^4
 \le C mL_n(K)^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, a union bound applied to the sub-Gaussian tails of
\(\epsilon_q\), and to the Gaussian comparison summands used in the cited
theorem, gives its upper function the bound
\[
 u(\gamma)\le C\sqrt mL_n(K)
 \sqrt{\log(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)}.
\]
If \(p=2\), duplicate either sign-expanded coordinate; this leaves the maximum
unchanged and permits the cited theorem's convention \(p\ge3\).  Substitution
in Theorem 2.2 of that source yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_z|P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|\le z\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}|\\
 &\quad\le C\left[
 m^{-1/8}(M_3^{3/4}\vee M_4^{1/2})
 \log^{7/8}(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)
 +m^{-1/2}\log^{3/2}(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)u(\gamma)+\gamma\right]\\
 &\quad\le\mathfrak g_n(\gamma),
 \end{aligned}
\]
because the first term is bounded by
\(C\{L_n(K)^2\log^7(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)\}^{1/8}\) and the second by
\(CL_n(K)\log^2(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)\).  No lower eigenvalue of
\(\Sigma_n\) is used: only the unit coordinate variances enter the cited
theorem.

We next transfer from the linear statistic to feasible studentization.  Put
\(t_k=\widehat s_k/s_k\).  By
\(\texttt{thm:uniform-influence}\), on \(\mathcal A_n(C)\),
\[
 \max_k|\rho_{n,k}|\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]
By \(\texttt{thm:heteroskedastic-covariance}\), on
\(\mathcal B_n(h)\), \(|t_k^2-1|\le\delta_h\).  When
\(\delta_h\le1/2\), the proof of that theorem also gives
\(t_k\ge\sqrt{1-\delta_h}\) and
\(|t_k^{-1}-1|\le\delta_h\).  Hence, on the intersection of the two events,
the reverse triangle inequality yields
\[
 \left|
 \max_k|t_k^{-1}(S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k})|-\max_k|S_{n,k}|
 \right|
 \le\delta_h\max_k|S_{n,k}|
 +\sqrt2C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]

The same sub-Gaussian moment-generating-function calculation used above,
now with \(\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1\), gives, for \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|>C_4\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}\}\le\delta_h
\]
after choosing \(C_4\) depending only on \(C_e\).  On the complementary
event the preceding perturbation is at most
\[
 v_n=C_5\{\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}
 +C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\}.
\]
Corollary 2.1 of
\(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-anti-concentration}\), applied to the finite
sign-expanded Gaussian vector with unit marginal variances, gives
\[
 \sup_zP\{|M_n^Z-z|\le v_n\}
 \le C_6v_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}.
\]
Sandwiching the feasible event between the linear events with thresholds
\(z-v_n\) and \(z+v_n\), and then using the already proved Gaussian
approximation, incurs the tail probability \(\delta_h\) and the
anti-concentration term
\[
 C_7\left\{C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}
 +\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)\log(2p)}\right\}.
\]
For \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\), elementary logarithm bounds give
\[
 \delta_h+\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)\log(2p)}
 \le C_8\left[\delta_h\log(2p)
 +\delta_h^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}\right].
\]
Indeed, use \(\sqrt{ab}\le a\) for \(a\ge b>0\), split
\(\log(2p/\delta_h)\), and use
\(x\log(1/x)\le Cx^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/x)\}^{2/3}\) on
\(0<x\le1/2\).  Enlarging \(C_3\) in the definition of
\(\mathfrak c_n(h)\) therefore proves
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_z\left|P_n\!\left\{
 \max_k\frac{|\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}|}{\widehat s_k}\le z
 \right\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|\\
 &\quad\le\mathfrak g_n(\gamma)+P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 +P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\\
 &\qquad+C_2\{C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}
 +\delta_h\log(2p)\}+\mathfrak c_n(h).
 \end{aligned}
\]

For the multiplier part, conditional on \(Y\), Gaussianity and independence
of \(\xi_q\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_k}\xi_q,
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{k'q}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_{k'}}\xi_q
 \mathrel{\Big|}Y\right)
 =\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}.
\]
Thus \(W_n^\xi\), conditionally on the data, is exactly the maximum absolute
coordinate of \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), the
covariance theorem gives
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
 \le\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}\le4\delta_h.
\]
Applying \(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-comparison-maxima}\) to the two
sign-expanded Gaussian vectors gives
\[
 \sup_z|P(W_n^\xi\le z\mid Y)-P(M_n^Z\le z)|
 \le C_3\delta_h^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}.
\]
The cited comparison permits singular covariance matrices and therefore
retains the full staircase dependence.

Let \(F_Z\) be the distribution function of \(M_n^Z\).  The cited
anti-concentration inequality implies that \(F_Z\) is continuous.  On
\(\mathcal B_n(h)\), if \(\mathfrak c_n(h)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\), the
conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(W_n^\xi\) lies between the
\((1-\alpha-\mathfrak c_n(h))\)- and
\((1-\alpha+\mathfrak c_n(h))\)-quantiles of \(F_Z\).  Apply the feasible
distribution bound at these two deterministic quantiles and lose at most
\(P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\) once more.  The observed-statistic bound already
contains one copy of \(\mathfrak c_n(h)\), and the quantile comparison adds a
second.  This proves the displayed finite coverage inequality.  When \(h=0\),
the scale perturbation and covariance discrepancy are exactly zero, so the
same conclusions hold with \(\mathfrak c_n(0)=0\) by direct substitution.

Finally, \(\texttt{ass:cell-leverage}\) implies
\(L_n(K)^2\log^7(pm)\to0\).  One may choose \(\gamma_n\downarrow0\) slowly
enough that
\(L_n(K)^2\log^7(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma_n)\to0\); the preceding formula then
shows \(\mathfrak g_n(\gamma_n)\to0\).  Assumption
\(\texttt{ass:uniform-remainder-envelope}\) gives
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}\to0\).  If
\(h_n\log^2(2p)\to0\), then \(\delta_{h_n}\log(2p)\to0\) and
\[
 \delta_{h_n}\log^2(p/\delta_{h_n})\to0,
\]
because both \(x\log^2(1/x)\to0\) as \(x\downarrow0\) and the assumed
\(\delta_{h_n}\log^2(2p)\to0\) hold.  Hence
\(\mathfrak c_n(h_n)\to0\).  Together with the two explicitly assumed
failure-probability limits, every term in the finite bound vanishes, proving
the conditional corollary and no stronger one.
